definition_zh: 使用；利用；消耗；用掉；对待
definition_en: to do something with a tool or thing for a purpose, or to take and consume something
core_image: 伸手把工具从抽屉里拿出来握在手中
scene: 厨房的抽屉一拉开，里面躺着各式各样的工具，母亲总能顺手拿出合适的那个。A good cook knows how to use every pot in the kitchen.
sceneCN: 这里 use 是「使用、利用」（第 1 个义项：拿工具去做事）；句意为好厨师懂得使用厨房里的每一口锅。伸手取工具的这幅画面，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 动词加 -er 构成，义为「用户；使用者」
加名词后缀 -age 构成，义为「用法；使用量」
加 -ful 构成，义为「有用的」
加 -less 构成，义为「无用的」
加 -able 构成，义为「可用的」

senses.title: To employ a thing for a purpose
senses.definition: to do something with a tool, object, or method in order to achieve a result
senses.definitionCN: 为了达到某个结果而用工具、物品或方法去做事
senses.example: She used a sharp knife to cut the bread.
senses.exampleCN: 她用一把快刀切面包。
senses.why: The verb names the act of taking something into one's hands and making it serve a purpose.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初就指「把东西拿到手里，让它为自己办事」，取用工具的意象就是它的本义。

senses.title: To spend or consume a supply
senses.definition: to consume an amount of something such as time, money, or fuel
senses.definitionCN: 消耗掉一定量的时间、金钱或燃料等
senses.example: The old truck uses a lot of fuel.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆旧卡车很费油。
senses.why: Whatever is put to work is partly spent in the process, so the same verb comes to mean using up a supply.
senses.whyCN: 东西一旦被动用来干活，过程中总要耗掉一部分，于是同一个动词就引申为「耗用」。

senses.title: The act or purpose of employing something
senses.definition: as a noun, the act of employing something or the purpose it serves
senses.definitionCN: 作名词时指使用的行为，或某物所起的作用
senses.example: This room is for the use of guests only.
senses.exampleCN: 这个房间仅供客人使用。
senses.why: The nouns formed from the verb simply name the action itself and the end it serves.
senses.whyCN: 由这个动词转成的名词只是把「使用」这个动作本身和它所服务的目的命名下来。

senses.title: To treat someone in a particular way
senses.definition: to behave towards somebody in a stated manner, often unfairly
senses.definitionCN: 以某种方式对待某人，常含有不公平的意味
senses.example: He felt that his boss had used him badly.
senses.exampleCN: 他觉得老板待他很刻薄。
senses.why: To use people is to treat them as tools; from that picture the verb widens into simply meaning to treat.
senses.whyCN: 把人当工具使，就是把对方当成器物；从这个画面出发，词义又扩大到泛指的「对待」。

senses.title: To take a drug or apply a substance
senses.definition: to take a drug, medicine, or other substance regularly or deliberately
senses.definitionCN: 有意识地、经常地服用药物或使用某种物质
senses.example: The doctor told him to use the cream twice a day.
senses.exampleCN: 医生让他每天涂两次这种药膏。
senses.why: Medicine is a supply applied to the body for a result, so it slips naturally into the same frame.
senses.whyCN: 药物就是施用于身体、换取疗效的东西，于是它自然套进了同一个句法框架。

intro.en: A short word from Old French, ultimately from Latin, that has kept its shape almost unchanged for eight centuries.
intro.cn: 一个来自古法语、最终可溯至拉丁语的小词，八百年来词形几乎没有变化。

items.en: Usus, the past participle of uti, meant a using or a practice, and usare was a frequentative form of the same verb.
items.cn: usus 是 uti 的过去分词，意为「使用、惯行」；usare 是同一动词的反复体形式。

items.en: Us, user, and the past participle usé carried the verb into everyday French for using and wearing out.
items.cn: us、user 以及过去分词 usé 把这个动词带进日常法语，兼表「使用」与「用旧」。

items.en: English borrows the verb in the thirteenth century as usen, with the noun use beside it.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪以 usen 的形式借入这个动词，名词 use 并行存在。

items.en: Spelling settles on use, and the word already covers tools, supplies, and medicine.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 use，词义这时已覆盖工具、物资与药物。

items.en: The question what is this used for turns the verb and noun into the commonest way of asking about purpose.
items.cn: what is this used for 这类问句让动词和名词成为询问用途最常用的手段。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the close relatives of the verb, while the near-meaning group sets tools against overuse and waste.
note.cn: 形近组收集这个动词的近亲，近义组则把使用与误用、滥用、浪费放在一起对照。

entries.definition: the way a word or thing is used
to use a tool or method
to use something badly or cruelly
to spend without any useful result

normalIntro.en: Three letters that name the everyday act of taking a thing and making it work for you.
normalIntro.cn: 三个字母，命名的是日常里把东西拿来替你办事的动作。

normal.en: Use up means finish the supply, as in use up all the paper.
normal.cn: use up 表示把存货用尽，如 use up all the paper。

normal.en: Make use of is the fixed phrase for turning something to your advantage.
normal.cn: make use of 是「加以利用」的固定说法。

normal.en: In use describes a machine that is working at this moment.
normal.cn: in use 形容机器此刻正在使用中。

normal.en: The noun use is pronounced with a soft s, the verb with a hard z.
normal.cn: 名词 use 末尾读清音 s，动词则读浊音 z。

normal.en: User, usage, useful, and useless all sit on this same short base.
normal.cn: user、usage、useful、useless 都建立在这个短词干上。

abstract.en: Picture a drawer of knives and spoons, and a hand closing on exactly the right one.
abstract.cn: 想象一抽屉的刀叉勺子，一只手正好抓住了对的那一件。

abstract.en: Feel the grip of a handle that many other hands have worn smooth.
abstract.cn: 体会一只被许多只手磨得光滑的把手。

abstract.en: Watch a full jar of coffee slowly empty day after day.
abstract.cn: 看着满满一罐咖啡一天天空下去。

examples.en: She used an old spoon to dig a hole for the seeds.
examples.cn: 她用一把旧勺子挖了个坑埋种子。

examples.en: We used up all the firewood before the snow came.
examples.cn: 雪落下之前我们把木柴都用光了。

examples.en: Learning to use a map is still a useful skill on long hikes.
examples.cn: 学会用地图在长途徒步中仍是一项有用的技能。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「优使」——把最好用的工具交给能干的人去使用。

root: 拉丁语 uti（使用）及其过去分词 usus、反复体 usare，经古法语 us / user 进入英语

sensesIntro.en: One act of taking a thing into service spreads to spending supplies, to the act itself, to treating people, and to taking medicine.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「把东西拿来用」这一个动作出发，词义扩展到耗用物资、使用行为、对待他人以及服用药物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand taking a tool and putting it to work.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手取出工具，让它开始干活。

branches.en: The tool branch: a thing made to serve a purpose.
branches.cn: 工具分支：让某物为某个目的服务。

branches.en: The supply branch: use eats into a store of fuel, money, or time.
branches.cn: 物资分支：使用会吃掉油、钱、时间的存量。

branches.en: The noun branch: the act itself and the purpose it serves.
branches.cn: 名词分支：使用这一行为以及它服务的目的。

branches.en: The people branch: treating someone as a tool.
branches.cn: 人事分支：把某人当作工具来对待。

branches.en: The medicine branch: a substance applied for a result.
branches.cn: 药物分支：为求疗效而施用的物质。

intro.en: The word is barely analysable today, but two Latin pieces are still readable behind it.
intro.cn: 这个词如今几乎无法拆分，但其背后仍能读出两个拉丁成分。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb uti, to use, gives usus and the frequentative usare; the short stem is all that survives in English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁动词 uti（使用）给出 usus 与反复体 usare，英语只留下了这条短词干。

items.example: The stem us- carries the whole idea of using.
items.exampleCN: 词干 us- 承载了「使用」的全部含义。

items.example: Use as a verb keeps a silent final e.
items.exampleCN: 作动词的 use 末尾有一个不发音的 e。

items.example: Use gives user, a person who uses.
items.exampleCN: use 加它成为 user，即使用者。

items.example: Usage means the way or amount of use.
items.exampleCN: usage 表示用法或使用量。

items.example: Use plus -ful gives useful.
Useless means without any use.
Usable means able to be used.
Misuse is the wrong kind of use.
Reuse means to use again.

definition_zh: 有用的；有益的；实用的
definition_en: helpful for doing something, or able to serve a practical purpose
core_image: 一把随身小刀，开箱、削果、割绳样样都行
scene: 出门前母亲往包里塞了一把折刀，说路上总会有用得着的时候。A small torch is really useful when the power fails.
sceneCN: 这里 useful 是「有用的」（第 1 个义项：能派上用场）；句意为停电时手电筒真的很有用。随身小刀件件都能用的画面，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 加 -ly 构成副词，义为「有用地；有益地」
加 -ness 构成名词，义为「有用性；实用性」
去掉后缀后的基础词，义为「使用」
换成否定后缀 -less，义为「无用的」

senses.title: Helpful for a practical purpose
senses.definition: able to help someone do something or reach a result
senses.definitionCN: 能够帮助某人做成某件事或达到某个结果
senses.example: Her advice was useful, and I changed my plan.
senses.exampleCN: 她的建议很有用，我因此改了计划。
senses.why: The base verb names putting a thing to work; the suffix means full of, so the adjective marks what is full of workable use.
senses.whyCN: 基础动词指「让东西干活」，后缀意为「充满」；所以这个词就是「充满可用之处」的东西。

senses.title: Worth keeping for later needs
senses.definition: described of a thing worth having because it will serve a need later
senses.definitionCN: 形容某物值得留着，因为日后会用得上
senses.example: Keep the box; it may come in useful when we move.
senses.exampleCN: 把箱子留着吧，搬家时也许用得上。
senses.why: A thing that can be put to work at any moment is worth keeping, and that practical judgement gives this sense.
senses.whyCN: 随时能拿来干活的东西自然值得保留，这层「留着有用」的实用判断由此产生。

senses.title: Producing good effects on people
senses.definition: having a good effect on a person's knowledge, health, or work
senses.definitionCN: 对某人的知识、健康或工作产生良好作用
senses.example: The trip was useful for her spoken English.
senses.exampleCN: 这趟旅行对她的口语很有帮助。
senses.why: From tools the word extends to anything that leaves a person better off, such as a lesson or a habit.
senses.whyCN: 从器物再往外延伸，凡是让人变得更好的东西（如一堂课、一个习惯）也可以这样形容。

senses.title: Practical rather than beautiful
senses.definition: plain and practical in design rather than attractive
senses.definitionCN: 设计朴素实用而不追求好看
senses.example: The kitchen is small but useful, with everything within reach.
senses.exampleCN: 厨房不大却很实用，东西伸手就能够到。
senses.why: If a thing is judged by how well it works, plainness stops being a fault; this sense praises function over looks.
senses.whyCN: 既然以「好不好使」来评判，朴素就不算缺点；这层义项正是对功能的称赞。

intro.en: A native suffix, full of, laid over the borrowed verb use; the compound has been in English since the Middle Ages.
intro.cn: 一个本土后缀「充满」压在借入的动词 use 之上，这个复合词在中古英语时期就已存在。

items.en: The suffix -full meant full or complete and was freely added to nouns.
items.cn: 后缀 -full 意为「满的、完全的」，可自由加在名词之后。

items.en: The base goes back to uti and its participle usus, a using.
items.cn: 词基可溯至 uti 及其分词 usus，意为「使用」。

items.en: Us and user carried the verb into French and from there into English.
items.cn: us 与 user 把这个动词带进法语，再进入英语。

items.en: Use and the suffix -ful combine, and the final l is later dropped in spelling.
items.cn: use 与后缀 -ful 结合，后来拼写中省去了末尾的一个 l。

items.en: Useful settles into the standard form, and usefully and usefulness follow it.
items.cn: useful 固定为标准写法，usefully 与 usefulness 相继派生。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the same use stem, and the near-meaning group sorts helpful words by strength.
note.cn: 形近组汇集同一 use 词干上的词，近义组按程度给「有帮助」一类的词排序。

entries.definition: to employ something for a purpose

normalIntro.en: Read it as use plus full: full of use, therefore worth having at hand.
normalIntro.cn: 把它读成 use 加 full：充满用处，因此值得随手带着。

normal.en: Use plus -ful follows the same pattern as helpful and careful.
normal.cn: use 加 -ful 与 helpful、careful 走的是同一构词路子。

normal.en: Come in useful is the idiom for something that turns out handy later.
normal.cn: come in useful 是「后来派上用场」的惯用说法。

normal.en: The negative partner is useless, with -less instead of -ful.
normal.cn: 否定形式是 useless，用的是 -less 而不是 -ful。

normal.en: Usefulness and usefully show the noun and adverb built on the same stem.
normal.cn: usefulness 与 usefully 是同词干上的名词和副词。

normal.en: In British spelling the word has one l before the end.
normal.cn: 英式拼写里这个词中间只有一个 l。

abstract.en: Picture a pocket knife that opens boxes, peels fruit, and cuts string.
abstract.cn: 想象一把小折刀，开箱、削果、割绳样样能干。

abstract.en: Hear a stranger say that your note saved them an afternoon.
abstract.cn: 听陌生人说，你那页笔记替他们省了一个下午。

abstract.en: Feel a torch click on in a sudden blackout.
abstract.cn: 体会突然停电时手电筒咔哒一声亮起。

examples.en: The leaflet gives useful advice on saving water at home.
examples.cn: 这份传单给了在家节水的有用建议。

examples.en: A folding chair is useful when guests arrive suddenly.
examples.cn: 客人突然来时折叠椅就派得上用场。

examples.en: He found the grammar notes useful before the exam.
examples.cn: 考试前他觉得那些语法笔记很有用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「优思否」——一样东西好不好用，先想一想它能不能替你省力。

root: 本土后缀 -ful（充满）加动词 use（源自拉丁语 uti / usus，经古法语 user），整体义为「充满用处」

sensesIntro.en: A core of full of use splits into practical help, keeping for later, good effects on people, and plain functional design.
sensesIntro.cn: 「充满用处」这个核心分成四路：实际帮助、留着备用、对人有益、朴素实用。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pocket knife that answers many needs.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把能应付多种需要的小折刀。

branches.en: The task branch: it helps the job get done.
branches.cn: 任务分支：它帮着把事情办成。

branches.en: The keeping branch: it earns a place in the drawer.
branches.cn: 留存分支：它值得占住抽屉的一角。

branches.en: The person branch: someone is better off after it.
branches.cn: 对人的分支：有了它，人变得更好。

branches.en: The design branch: plain looks judged by how well it works.
branches.cn: 设计分支：朴素的外表以好不好使来评判。

branches.en: The judgement branch: worth is measured by future help.
branches.cn: 评判分支：价值按它日后能帮多少来衡量。

intro.en: A Germanic adjective suffix on a borrowed verb: what is full of use is useful.
intro.cn: 日耳曼语形容词后缀加在借入的动词上：充满用处的，就是有用的。

latinIntro.en: The stem comes from Latin uti, to use, whose participle usus gave the noun use.
latinIntro.cn: 词干来自拉丁语 uti（使用），其分词 usus 给出名词 use。

items.example: Use the small spoon for sugar.
Useful means full of use.
Useless means without use.
Usefully describes how something helps.
items.exampleCN: usefully 说明有帮助地做事。

items.example: Usefulness names the quality itself.
items.exampleCN: usefulness 命名这种性质本身。

items.example: A user is one who uses.
Usage records how something is used.
A misuse is a wrong use.

definition_zh: 无用的；无效的；差劲的；无能为力的
definition_en: not able to serve any purpose, with no effect, or of very poor quality
core_image: 雨伞的伞骨全断了，撑开只剩一块破布
scene: 雨下得正急，他打开那把旧伞，伞骨立刻折断，雨水顺着脖子流下来。The broken umbrella was completely useless in that storm.
sceneCN: 这里 useless 是「无用的、不顶事的」（第 1 个义项：起不到应有的作用）；句意为那把坏伞在那场暴雨中完全没用。伞骨尽断的画面，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 加 -ness 构成名词，义为「无用」
加 -ly 构成副词，义为「无用地」
换成肯定后缀 -ful，义为「有用的」
去掉后缀后的基础词，义为「使用」

senses.title: Unable to serve any purpose
senses.definition: not able to do what it is meant to do
senses.definitionCN: 做不到它本该做到的事情
senses.example: The old phone is useless because the screen will not turn on.
senses.exampleCN: 那部旧手机没用了，屏幕根本开不亮。
senses.why: The suffix -less means without, so the word simply says that no use can be found in the thing at all.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -less 意为「没有」，所以说得很直白：这东西里根本找不出用处。

senses.title: Having no effect on a result
senses.definition: producing no effect on the situation, however much effort is made
senses.definitionCN: 无论费多少力气，对局面都不产生任何影响
senses.example: Shouting at the referee was useless.
senses.exampleCN: 冲着裁判大喊毫无作用。
senses.why: If a tool cannot change anything, it is as good as broken; the same judgement passes to efforts and protests.
senses.whyCN: 工具改变不了任何事，就跟坏了一样；同样的判断于是也用在了努力与抗议上。

senses.title: Very poor in quality
senses.definition: used informally of something of very low quality or performance
senses.definitionCN: 口语中形容质量或表现极差
senses.example: This useless little fan does not cool the room at all.
senses.exampleCN: 这台破小风扇根本吹不凉屋子。
senses.why: Anything that fails to perform gets the label by a short step, and the word becomes ordinary slang for shoddy things.
senses.whyCN: 做不好事的东西很容易就被贴上这个标签，于是它也成了口语里形容蹩脚货的常用词。

senses.title: Unable to help or cope
senses.definition: describing a person who cannot help or deal with a situation
senses.definitionCN: 形容一个人帮不上忙、应付不了局面
senses.example: He felt useless while she packed for the move alone.
senses.exampleCN: 她一个人收拾搬家的东西时，他觉得很帮不上忙。
senses.why: A person whose hands cannot change things is like a broken tool, which is why the word also describes helpless feeling.
senses.whyCN: 一个人的手改变不了局面，就同一件坏工具无异；这层「感到无能为力」的用法由此而来。

intro.en: The native suffix -less, meaning without, added to the borrowed verb use; a plain negative compound.
intro.cn: 本土后缀 -less（意为「没有」）加在借入动词 use 之上，是一个直白的否定复合词。

items.en: The suffix -leas meant without or free from, as in homeless and hopeless.
items.cn: 后缀 -leas 意为「没有、免于」，如 homeless 与 hopeless 中的用法。

items.en: The base verb descends from uti and its participle usus, a using.
items.cn: 词基动词可溯至 uti 及其分词 usus，意为「使用」。

items.en: User and usé carried the verb through French into English.
items.cn: user 与 usé 把这个动词经法语带入英语。

items.en: Use joins the suffix so that useless names what has no use at all.
items.cn: use 与后缀结合，useless 便用来指毫无用处之物。

items.en: The sense widens to hopeless efforts and then to anything of poor quality.
items.cn: 词义扩大到徒劳的努力，继而扩展到任何质量低劣的东西。

note.en: The look-alike group is the same use stem with its negative suffix, and the near-meaning group lines up words for things that fail to work.
note.cn: 形近组是同一 use 词干加否定后缀，近义组则把「不起作用」一类词排成一列。

normalIntro.en: Use plus -less: without any use, and by a short step without any point.
normalIntro.cn: use 加 -less：没有用处，再往前一步就成了毫无意义。

normal.en: The pair useful and useless differ only in the suffix.
normal.cn: useful 与 useless 的区别只在那一个后缀上。

normal.en: Worse than useless means harmful as well as pointless.
normal.cn: worse than useless 指不但无用还有害。

normal.en: Uselessness is the noun, uselessly the adverb.
normal.cn: 名词是 uselessness，副词是 uselessly。

normal.en: The same -less pattern gives hopeless and careless.
normal.cn: hopeless、careless 走的是同一个 -less 模式。

normal.en: Feel useless describes a person, not a thing.
normal.cn: feel useless 描述的是人，而不是物。

abstract.en: Picture an umbrella whose ribs snap in the first gust of wind.
abstract.cn: 想象一把伞在第一阵风里就折断伞骨。

abstract.en: Hear yourself shouting advice that no one can hear.
abstract.cn: 听自己喊出的建议，没人听得见。

abstract.en: Hold a watch that has stopped at the same minute for years.
abstract.cn: 握着一只多年来始终停在同一分钟的表。

examples.en: Without a charger, the laptop is useless on the road.
examples.cn: 没有充电器，这台笔记本在路上派不上用场。

examples.en: Complaining after the decision proved a useless effort.
examples.cn: 决定之后再去抱怨，成了徒劳的力气。

examples.en: This useless pair of scissors cannot even cut paper.
examples.cn: 这把破剪刀连纸都剪不动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「优是劣」——表面看着优，一上手才发现是劣等货，全不管用。

root: 本土否定后缀 -less（没有）加动词 use（拉丁语 uti / usus，经古法语 user），义为「毫无用处」

sensesIntro.en: The core without any use spreads to efforts that change nothing, to shoddy goods, and to a person who cannot help.
sensesIntro.cn: 「毫无用处」这个核心扩展到改变不了局面的努力、粗劣的物品以及帮不上忙的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an umbrella with broken ribs in a downpour.
core.cn: 核心意象：倾盆大雨里一把断了伞骨的伞。

branches.en: The tool branch: it cannot do what it was made for.
branches.cn: 工具分支：它做不到自己该做的事。

branches.en: The effort branch: actions that leave the world unchanged.
branches.cn: 努力分支：行动过后局面毫无变化。

branches.en: The quality branch: shoddy goods in everyday speech.
branches.cn: 质量分支：口语里形容蹩脚货。

branches.en: The person branch: hands that can do nothing here.
branches.cn: 人身分支：一双手在此地帮不上任何忙。

branches.en: The judgement branch: no use and no effect are one verdict.
branches.cn: 评判分支：没用与无效其实是同一个判词。

intro.en: A negating Germanic suffix on a borrowed verb: without any use.
intro.cn: 日耳曼语否定后缀加在借入动词上：一点用处也没有。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Latin uti and its participle usus; the negative suffix itself is not Latin but native English.
latinIntro.cn: 词干是拉丁语 uti 及其分词 usus；否定后缀本身并非拉丁语，而是英语本土成分。

items.example: Use the back door, not the front.
Useless means without use.
Its opposite is useful.
Uselessness is the state of being useless.
He uselessly tried to fix it.
A user is a person who uses.

items.structure: base noun in the same pattern
items.example: Hopeless uses the same suffix.
items.exampleCN: hopeless 用的是同一个后缀。

items.structure: base noun in the same pattern
items.example: Careless also shows -less at work.
items.exampleCN: careless 同样展示了 -less 的用法。

definition_zh: 用户；使用者；服用者
definition_en: a person or thing that uses something, especially a person who uses a service or product
core_image: 一个人低头在手机上一步步按着界面操作
scene: 图书馆新装的借书机前，年轻人排队试着操作，工作人员在一旁教第一次来的读者。Every new user needs a minute to learn the screen.
sceneCN: 这里 user 是「使用者、用户」（第 1 个义项：使用某物或某项服务的人）；句意为每个新用户都需要一点时间熟悉这块屏幕。低头操作界面的画面，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 去掉后缀后的动词，义为「使用」
同族名词，义为「用法；使用量」
复合形容词，义为「易于使用的」
加 -able 的同族形容词，义为「可用的」

senses.title: A person who uses a product or service
senses.definition: someone who uses a product, service, or system, especially regularly
senses.definitionCN: 使用某产品、服务或系统的人，尤指经常使用的人
senses.example: The website asks every user to choose a password.
senses.exampleCN: 网站要求每位用户设置一个密码。
senses.why: The verb names the act of putting something to work; adding the agent suffix marks the person doing it.
senses.whyCN: 动词指「让东西干活」，加上表人的后缀，就指做这件事的那个人。

senses.title: Someone who takes drugs
senses.definition: a person who takes a drug, often habitually
senses.definitionCN: 服用药物的人，常指长期吸食毒品者
senses.example: The clinic helps long-term drug users rebuild their lives.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所帮助长期吸毒的人重建生活。
senses.why: A drug is also something taken into the body, so the same word carries over to the person who takes it.
senses.whyCN: 药物同样是进入身体的东西，于是这个词也延伸到了服用它的人身上。

senses.title: A device or person consuming a resource
senses.definition: a person or organisation that consumes water, power, or another supply
senses.definitionCN: 消耗水、电或其他资源的个人或机构
senses.example: The village is the largest water user in the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村子是山谷里用水最多的一方。
senses.why: Since use also means spending a supply, an agent noun can describe whoever draws on that supply.
senses.whyCN: 既然 use 还有「耗用」之义，表人的名词自然也能指取用这份资源的那一方。

senses.title: A person skilled in handling something
senses.definition: a person who knows how to handle a tool or a situation well
senses.definitionCN: 懂得把工具或局面用得熟练的人
senses.example: He is a skilful user of words, able to calm any room.
senses.exampleCN: 他很会用词，能让任何场合安静下来。
senses.why: The same agent noun can praise skill, because the one who uses a thing well is the one who masters it.
senses.whyCN: 同一个表人名词也能表示赞赏：把东西用得好的人，就是掌握它的人。

intro.en: The agent suffix -er, native to English, added to the borrowed verb use.
intro.cn: 英语本土的表人后缀 -er 加在借入动词 use 之上。

items.en: The suffix -ere made agent nouns, as in writer and baker, and is still fully productive.
items.cn: 后缀 -ere 构成表人名词，如 writer、baker，至今仍能自由造词。

items.en: The base comes from uti, to use, with its participle usus.
items.cn: 词基来自 uti（使用）及其分词 usus。

items.en: The verb reached English through French as user, to use.
items.cn: 这个动词经法语 user（使用）进入英语。

items.en: User appears early for anyone who uses a thing, with no link to machines.
items.cn: user 早期泛指使用某物的人，与机器无关。

items.en: With computers and the internet the word becomes the standard term for the person at the screen.
items.cn: 随着电脑与互联网的普及，这个词成为指屏幕前那个人的标准说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the use family, and the near-meaning group names people in terms of what they consume or control.
note.cn: 形近组汇集 use 词族，近义组则从消耗或掌控的角度来称呼人。

entries.definition: a person who buys and uses goods
a person who buys from a shop
a person who works a machine
a person or firm that supplies a service

normalIntro.en: A plain agent noun: the one who uses is the user, exactly as a writer writes.
normalIntro.cn: 一个朴素的表人名词：谁是用的那个人，谁就是 user，正如写的人叫 writer。

normal.en: User follows the writer and baker pattern of verb plus -er.
normal.cn: user 走的是 writer、baker 那样「动词加 -er」的路子。

normal.en: User name and password are fixed pairs in every login box.
normal.cn: user name 与 password 是每个登录框里的固定搭配。

normal.en: Heavy user suggests a habit, while first-time user suggests novelty.
normal.cn: heavy user 暗示习惯，first-time user 暗示初次接触。

normal.en: The adjective is user-friendly, a modern compound.
normal.cn: 形容词形式是 user-friendly，属于现代复合词。

normal.en: Drug user is a medical or social term, not a technical one.
normal.cn: drug user 是医学或社会用语，并非技术术语。

abstract.en: Picture a queue at a self-service machine, each person learning the screen.
abstract.cn: 想象自助机前排着队，每个人都在学怎么用那块屏幕。

abstract.en: Hear the click of a login page opening on a phone.
abstract.cn: 听手机上一声轻响，登录页弹出。

abstract.en: See worn spots on a keyboard where the same fingers always land.
abstract.cn: 看键盘上被同一副手指磨出来的那几处。

examples.en: Each user of the shared bike must lock it afterwards.
examples.cn: 每位共享单车用户都必须之后锁好车。

examples.en: The guide was written for users with no technical training.
examples.cn: 这本指南是写给没有技术背景的使用者的。

examples.en: A heavy user of electricity will notice the bill at once.
examples.cn: 用电大户立刻就能感到账单的变化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「优择」——挑来挑去，最后选中使用的就是用户。

root: 本土表人后缀 -er 加动词 use（拉丁语 uti / usus，经古法语 user），义为「使用的人」

sensesIntro.en: One agent noun branches from using products to taking drugs, from drawing on a supply to mastering a skill.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个表人名词，从使用产品分到吸食药物，从耗用资源分到精于此道。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person at a screen, learning how it works.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人面对着屏幕，熟悉它的用法。

branches.en: The product branch: the person a service is built for.
branches.cn: 产品分支：服务所围绕的那个人。

branches.en: The drug branch: the body as the thing being used.
branches.cn: 药物分支：身体成了被使用的对象。

branches.en: The resource branch: whoever draws water or power.
branches.cn: 资源分支：取水取电的那一方。

branches.en: The skill branch: skill turns a user into a master.
branches.cn: 技艺分支：熟练使使用者变成行家。

branches.en: The consumption branch: using always takes something up.
branches.cn: 消耗分支：凡是使用总要占用掉一些什么。

intro.en: A verb plus the native agent suffix: the person who performs the action.
intro.cn: 动词加本土表人后缀：执行这个动作的人。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin uti and its participle usus; the suffix -er is Germanic, not Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 uti 及其分词 usus；-er 后缀是日耳曼语成分，不是拉丁语。

items.example: Use both hands on the wheel.
A user is one who uses.
Usage is the way of using.
Useful is built on the same base.
items.exampleCN: useful 也建在同一词基上。

items.example: Usable means able to be used.
User-friendly is a modern blend.
A writer is the matching agent noun.
items.exampleCN: writer 是同构的表人名词。

items.example: A baker shows -er at work again.
items.exampleCN: baker 再次显示 -er 的作用。

definition_zh: 通常的；平常的；一贯的；惯常的
definition_en: happening or done most of the time, and therefore normal for a person or place
core_image: 每天早上七点同一个座位上一杯同样的咖啡
scene: 清晨的小店刚开门，靠窗那张桌子已经坐上了熟客，点的还是那杯不加水的美式。He sat at his usual table and ordered the same coffee.
sceneCN: 这里 usual 是「通常的、惯常的」（第 1 个义项：多数时候都如此）；句意为老顾客坐着他常坐的那张桌子，喝着常点的咖啡。每天早上同一杯咖啡的画面，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 加 -ly 构成副词，义为「通常；一般」
加否定前缀 un-，义为「不寻常的」
同根动词，义为「使用」
同根名词，义为「用法；惯例」

senses.title: What normally happens
senses.definition: describing what happens most often or is most often seen
senses.definitionCN: 形容最常发生或最常见的情况
senses.example: The usual bus is ten minutes late in the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 下雨时那班常坐的公交总会晚十分钟。
senses.why: The Latin source names what custom has made habitual, and habit is simply what happens most of the time.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的拉丁来源指「习俗使之成为常态的东西」，而习惯也就是大多数时候都会发生的事。

senses.title: Customary for one person or place
senses.definition: describing a fixed habit of one particular person, family, or shop
senses.definitionCN: 形容某个人、家庭或店铺固定不变的习惯
senses.example: She took her usual walk along the river after dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 晚饭后她照例沿着河走一走。
senses.why: Custom is personal as well as general, so the word also marks the private routines that repeat every day.
senses.whyCN: 习俗既属于众人也属于个人，所以这个词也用来标记每天重复的私人习惯。

senses.title: The ordinary option in a shop
senses.definition: in informal speech, the food or drink one always orders
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指某人每次固定点的那份饮食
senses.example: The waiter brought him the usual without asking.
senses.exampleCN: 服务员问都没问就给他端来了老样子。
senses.why: Once a choice is repeated often enough, it becomes a name in itself, and people simply order the usual.
senses.whyCN: 一个选择重复得够多就成了它自己的名字，人们于是干脆说「老样子」。

senses.title: That is as expected, nothing new
senses.definition: used of an unpleasant event that is exactly what one would expect
senses.definitionCN: 用于形容某件不愉快的事完全在意料之中
senses.example: His usual excuse was that the train was late again.
senses.exampleCN: 他还是那套老借口：火车又晚点了。
senses.why: Because habitual things are predictable, the word easily carries a faint tone of weary expectation.
senses.whyCN: 惯常之事总是可预料的，于是这个词也容易带上一丝厌烦的「又是这样」的意味。

intro.en: From Latin through French: a word about custom and habit, whose base is shared with use.
intro.cn: 经由法语来自拉丁语：一个关于习俗与习惯的词，其词基与 use 同源。

items.en: Usus meant use, practice, and custom; usualis described what custom made ordinary.
items.cn: usus 意为使用、实践与习俗；usualis 形容习俗使之成为常态的事物。

items.en: The form usualis is recorded as an adjective of everyday practice.
items.cn: usualis 这一形式有记录，用作指日常实践的形容词。

items.en: Usuel and the learned usual entered French usage alongside the everyday us.
items.cn: usuel 与书面形式 usual 同日常的 us 一起在法语中并行。

items.en: Usual enters English in the fourteenth century, first in legal and church writing.
items.cn: usual 于十四世纪进入英语，最早见于法律与教会文书。

items.en: The everyday phrases as usual and business as usual make the word home in ordinary speech.
items.cn: as usual 与 business as usual 这些日常说法让这个词彻底扎根于口语。

note.en: The look-alike group shows the use family behind usual, and the near-meaning group gathers words for what is normal.
note.cn: 形近组展示 usual 背后的 use 词族，近义组汇集表示「正常」的一类词。

normalIntro.en: Think of custom turned into an adjective: what a person or place always does.
normalIntro.cn: 把「习俗」变成形容词来想：某个人或某个地方总是这么做。

normal.en: As usual is a two-word phrase meaning in the normal way.
normal.cn: as usual 是两个词组成的短语，意为「像平常一样」。

normal.en: Business as usual says that nothing has changed.
normal.cn: business as usual 表示一切照旧。

normal.en: The adverb usually is far more frequent in speech than the adjective.
normal.cn: 副词 usually 在口语中比形容词本身常用得多。

normal.en: Unusual is the common opposite, formed with un-.
normal.cn: unusual 是用 un- 构成的常见反义词。

normal.en: Usual shares its root with use and usage.
normal.cn: usual 与 use、usage 同根。

abstract.en: Picture the same window seat taken every morning at seven.
abstract.cn: 想象每天早上七点都占着同一个靠窗座位。

abstract.en: Hear a waiter say the usual before you sit down.
abstract.cn: 听服务员在你落座前就说「老样子」。

abstract.en: Notice a worn path across the grass where everyone walks.
abstract.cn: 留意草地上被大家踩出来的一条小径。

examples.en: As usual, she arrived ten minutes before the meeting began.
examples.cn: 像往常一样，她在会议开始前十分钟就到了。

examples.en: He ordered his usual soup and read the paper.
examples.cn: 他点了常喝的那份汤，看着报纸。

examples.en: The shop keeps its usual hours even during the holiday.
examples.cn: 假期里这家店也保持着平常的营业时间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「优若」——习惯的事做起来总是优若自然，不必多想。

root: 拉丁语 usus（使用、实践、习俗）派生 usualis，经古法语 usuel / usual 进入英语，义为「按习俗常行的」

sensesIntro.en: From custom comes what happens most of the time, then personal routines, then the fixed order, and finally the weary expected excuse.
sensesIntro.cn: 从习俗出发，先指多数时候发生的事，再指个人日常、固定点单，最后是那句听腻了的预料之中的借口。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the same seat and the same coffee every morning.
core.cn: 核心意象：每天早上同一张座位、同一杯咖啡。

branches.en: The habit branch: what happens on most days.
branches.cn: 习惯分支：大多数日子都会发生的事。

branches.en: The person branch: this family or shop always does so.
branches.cn: 个体分支：这一家、这一店总是如此。

branches.en: The order branch: the dish repeated until it has a name.
branches.cn: 点单分支：重复到有了名字的那份菜。

branches.en: The excuse branch: expected, and therefore tiring.
branches.cn: 借口分支：全然预料之中，因此令人厌倦。

branches.en: The expectation branch: habit makes events predictable.
branches.cn: 预期分支：习惯让事情变得可以预测。

intro.en: An adjective ending on a stem shared with use, formed in Latin and polished in French.
intro.cn: 一个形容词，接在与 use 同源的词干上，成形于拉丁语，经法语打磨。

latinIntro.en: Latin usus, use and custom, yields the adjective usualis, whose ending -alis becomes English -al.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 usus（使用与习俗）派生出形容词 usualis，其词尾 -alis 变成英语的 -al。

items.example: The stem us- carries the idea of custom.
items.exampleCN: 词干 us- 承载「习俗」之义。

items.example: Usual means related to custom.
Usually marks what happens in the normal way.
items.exampleCN: usually 标记按常规发生的事。

items.example: Unusual means not customary.
Usualness is rarely needed in speech.
items.exampleCN: usualness 在口语中很少用到。

items.example: Use and usual share one root.
Usage records what custom accepts.
items.exampleCN: usage 记录习俗所认可的说法。

items.example: Custom is the plain English partner.
items.exampleCN: custom 是这个词朴素的英语伙伴。

definition_zh: 通常；经常；一般；照例
definition_en: in most cases, or on most occasions
core_image: 一年里绝大多数早晨，同一扇窗在同一个时刻亮起
scene: 邻居家那盏厨房灯总是六点半准时亮起，只有停电那天例外。She usually leaves for work before the streets get busy.
sceneCN: 这里 usually 是「通常、一般」（第 1 个义项：多数情况下如此）；句意为她一般在街上还没忙起来时就出门上班。每天同一时刻亮起的厨房灯，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -ly 后的形容词，义为「通常的；平常的」
加否定前缀 un-，义为「不寻常地」
同根动词，义为「使用」
同根名词，义为「用法；惯例」

senses.title: In most cases
senses.definition: used to say what happens in the majority of situations
senses.definitionCN: 用来说明在大多数情形下会发生什么
senses.example: Trains here usually run on time.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的火车通常准点运行。
senses.why: The adjective names what custom makes normal; the adverb turns that frequency into a statement about how often things happen.
senses.whyCN: 形容词指习俗使之成为常态的东西，加 -ly 成副词后，就把这种「常态」变成对发生频率的说明。

senses.title: As a settled habit
senses.definition: used of a person's regular practice rather than of things in general
senses.definitionCN: 用于说明某个人一贯的做法，而不是泛指一般情况
senses.example: He usually walks to the office unless it rains.
senses.exampleCN: 除非下雨，他通常走着去办公室。
senses.why: Habits are personal customs, so the adverb also marks what a particular person always does.
senses.whyCN: 习惯属于个人的习俗，因此这个副词也用来标记某个人一贯的做法。

senses.title: Generally true, with exceptions
senses.definition: weakening a general statement so that exceptions are allowed
senses.definitionCN: 用来弱化一个概括说法，为例外留出余地
senses.example: Books like this are usually written for beginners.
senses.exampleCN: 这类书一般是写给初学者的。
senses.why: Because custom holds most of the time rather than always, the adverb naturally signals a rule with exceptions.
senses.whyCN: 习俗只是多数时候成立而非绝对，所以这个副词天然带上「大体如此、但有例外」的语气。

senses.title: In the normal place or condition
senses.definition: used to state where or in what state something is normally found
senses.definitionCN: 用于说明某物通常出现在何处或以何种状态存在
senses.example: The keys are usually in the drawer by the door.
senses.exampleCN: 钥匙一般在门边的抽屉里。
senses.why: A fixed routine creates a fixed place for things, so the adverb also answers the everyday question of where something normally is.
senses.whyCN: 固定的习惯会为东西定下固定的位置，于是这个副词也用来回答「东西一般放在哪儿」。

intro.en: The adverb formed from usual with the native suffix -ly; behind it lies Latin usus, custom.
intro.cn: 由 usual 加本土副词后缀 -ly 构成，背后是拉丁语 usus（习俗）。

items.en: Usus meant use, practice, and custom, and usualis described what custom made ordinary.
items.cn: usus 意为使用、实践与习俗，usualis 形容习俗使之成为常态的事物。

items.en: Usuel carried the adjective into French, where adverbs were already regularly made with a -ment or -ment/-ly pattern.
items.cn: usuel 把形容词带进法语，当时的副词已有固定的构成方式。

items.en: The adjective usual arrives in the fourteenth century and the adverb usually follows in the fifteenth.
items.cn: 形容词 usual 于十四世纪进入英语，副词 usually 于十五世纪随后出现。

items.en: Usually grows into one of the most frequent sentence adverbs in written and spoken English.
items.cn: usually 逐渐成为书面与口语中最常见的句子副词之一。

items.en: Newspaper style prefers usually to the longer phrase in most cases.
items.cn: 报刊文体更爱用 usually，而不写较长的 in most cases。

note.en: The look-alike group is the usual family with its suffixes, and the near-meaning group ranks frequency adverbs.
note.cn: 形近组是 usual 词族及其后缀形式，近义组把表示频率的副词按高低排开。

entries.definition: in a way that is not normal
in a relaxed way, only the spelling looks close, the root is different
entries.definitionCN: 随意地；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: in most cases, on the whole

normalIntro.en: Take the adjective of custom and add the plain adverb ending; what is usual happens usually.
normalIntro.cn: 把表示习俗的形容词加上最普通的副词词尾：usual 的事就 usually 发生。

normal.en: Usually sits mid-sentence, before the main verb: usually runs, usually walks.
normal.cn: usually 常位于句中主要动词之前，如 usually runs、usually walks。

normal.en: The negative partner is unusually, not rarely.
normal.cn: 它的否定形式是 unusually，而不是 rarely。

normal.en: Usually before a general subject talks about things, not people.
normal.cn: usually 与泛指主语连用时说的是事物，不是某个人。

normal.en: In formal writing the phrases tend to and as a rule compete with it.
normal.cn: 正式写作里 tend to 与 as a rule 与它竞争。

normal.en: Usual and usually share one stem with use and usage.
normal.cn: usual 与 usually 跟 use、usage 共用一个词干。

abstract.en: Picture a kitchen window lighting up at half past six every morning.
abstract.cn: 想象每天早上六点半亮起的那扇厨房窗。

abstract.en: Hear the same train announced on the same platform.
abstract.cn: 听同一站台反复播报同一趟车。

abstract.en: Notice the one day the shop shuts early, and remember it as the exception.
abstract.cn: 留意商店唯一一次提前关门，把它当作例外记住。

examples.en: I usually take the side road when the main street is jammed.
examples.cn: 主街堵车时我通常走小路。

examples.en: These birds are usually seen near water in winter.
examples.cn: 这些鸟冬天一般在近水处出现。

examples.en: She usually finishes her report before Friday.
examples.cn: 她一般在周五前就把报告写完。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「优若利」——习惯的事做起来总是优若顺利，不必费力。

root: 形容词 usual（拉丁语 usus / usualis，经古法语）加副词后缀 -ly，义为「按惯例地、通常」

sensesIntro.en: From custom in general the adverb moves to personal habit, to a rule with exceptions, and to the normal place of things.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一般的习俗出发，这个副词先指个人习惯，再指有例外的通则，最后指事物常处的位置。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one window lighting up at the same minute all year.
core.cn: 核心意象：一整年里同一分钟亮起的一扇窗。

branches.en: The frequency branch: this is what happens on most days.
branches.cn: 频率分支：大多数日子都是这样。

branches.en: The habit branch: one person's regular practice.
branches.cn: 习惯分支：某个人一贯的做法。

branches.en: The exception branch: a general truth that allows cases against it.
branches.cn: 例外分支：允许反面情况的概括之论。

branches.en: The place branch: the spot where things are normally found.
branches.cn: 位置分支：东西平常所在之处。

branches.en: The expectation branch: prediction with a margin of doubt.
branches.cn: 预期分支：留有疑问余地的预测。

intro.en: The most ordinary adverb ending in English laid on an adjective of custom.
intro.cn: 英语里最普通的副词词尾，加在一个表示习俗的形容词上。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Latin usus, custom and practice, with the adjective ending -alis becoming -al.
latinIntro.cn: 词干是拉丁语 usus（习俗、实践），形容词词尾 -alis 变成 -al。

items.example: The stem points to settled practice.
items.exampleCN: 词干指向固定下来的做法。

items.example: Usual means relating to custom.
Usually says in the customary way.
items.exampleCN: usually 表示按惯例的方式。

items.example: Unusually marks the rare case.
Use belongs to the same family.
Usage records what people usually say.
items.exampleCN: usage 记录人们通常怎么说。

items.example: Normally is a close rival adverb.
items.exampleCN: normally 是相近的竞争副词。

items.example: In most cases means much the same.
items.exampleCN: in most cases 意思相仿。

definition_zh: 效用；实用；公用事业；公共设施
definition_en: the quality of being useful, or a public service such as water, gas, or electricity
core_image: 墙上一排电表水表，各自记录着看不见的供给
scene: 老房子的墙角挂着一排水表电表，每月都有人来抄一次数字，账单随后寄到信箱。Water is the most basic utility in any city.
sceneCN: 这里 utility 是「公用事业」（第 3 个义项：水、电、燃气这类公共服务）；句意为水是任何城市最基本的公用事业。墙角一排计量表的画面，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 同根动词，义为「利用」
同根形容词，义为「功利的；实用的」
同根名词，义为「利用」
同源基础词，义为「使用」

senses.title: The quality of being useful
senses.definition: the quality of being useful or of practical value
senses.definitionCN: 有用或具有实际价值的性质
senses.example: The new tool's utility lies in its simple handle.
senses.exampleCN: 这件新工具的效用在于它那只简单的把手。
senses.why: The Latin noun joined utilis, useful, to the abstract ending -itas, so the word names usefulness as a measurable quality.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁名词由 utilis（有用的）加抽象词尾 -itas 构成，因此它把「有用」说成一种可以衡量的性质。

senses.title: The usefulness of something in a particular role
senses.definition: the particular purpose a thing can serve in practice
senses.definitionCN: 某物在实际情况中能充当的具体用途
senses.example: The old barn has lost its utility as a store.
senses.exampleCN: 那座旧谷仓已经失去了储藏方面的功用。
senses.why: From usefulness in general the word narrows to the specific job a thing can still do.
senses.whyCN: 从一般的有用性出发，词义收窄到某物还能承担的那项具体职能。

senses.title: A public service such as water or power
senses.definition: an organisation or service supplying water, gas, electricity, or similar necessities
senses.definitionCN: 供应水、燃气、电力等必需品的机构或服务
senses.example: The city raised utility prices for the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 市里提高了冬季的公用事业收费。
senses.why: Such services were seen as the most useful goods a town could own, so the abstract noun came to name the companies themselves.
senses.whyCN: 人们把这些服务看作城镇最该有的「有用之物」，于是这个抽象名词转而指供应它们的公司本身。

senses.title: A computer program for small tasks
senses.definition: a small program that performs a practical function in a computer system
senses.definitionCN: 在计算机系统中完成某项实用功能的小程序
senses.example: The disk utility found the damaged file.
senses.exampleCN: 磁盘工具程序找到了那个损坏的文件。
senses.why: Software borrowed the word for programs whose whole worth is practical, echoing the oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: 软件领域借用了这个词，指那些价值完全在于实用的程序，恰好回应了最古老的那层意思。

senses.title: In economics, the satisfaction goods give
senses.definition: in economics, the satisfaction or benefit a person gets from a good
senses.definitionCN: 经济学中个人从商品中获得的满足或益处
senses.example: Economists measure utility rather than price.
senses.exampleCN: 经济学家衡量的是效用，而不是价格。
senses.why: Economists made the abstract quality countable, turning usefulness into a quantity that choices can be weighed against.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家把这层抽象性质变得可以计量，让「有用」成为一种可供选择权衡的量。

intro.en: From Latin utilis, useful, through French; the abstract ending marks it as a noun of quality.
intro.cn: 来自拉丁语 utilis（有用的），经法语进入英语；抽象词尾表明它是一个表示性质的名词。

items.en: Utilis meant useful, from uti, to use, and utilitas named the quality just as bonitas named goodness.
items.cn: utilis 意为「有用的」，来自 uti（使用），utilitas 像 bonitas 表善那样表「有用」这种性质。

items.en: Utilité carried the abstract sense of usefulness into French legal and scholarly prose.
items.cn: utilité 把「有用性」这一抽象义带进法语的法律与学术文章。

items.en: Utility arrives in English in the fourteenth century, first meaning usefulness.
items.cn: utility 于十四世纪进入英语，最初只表示有用性。

items.en: From the nineteenth century, utility names the companies that supply water, gas, and power.
items.cn: 自十九世纪起，utility 用来指供应水、燃气与电力的公司。

items.en: Economics and computing each take the word for a measured benefit and for a practical program.
items.cn: 经济学与计算机领域各自取用这个词，表可计量的效用与实用的程序。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the util- family, and the near-meaning group places usefulness beside value and service.
note.cn: 形近组收集 util- 词族，近义组把有用性与价值、服务放在一起。

entries.definition: designed for use rather than beauty
plural, also the shares of such companies
entries.definitionCN: 公用事业；公用事业股票

entries.definition: a system supplying a public need

normalIntro.en: See util- as the useful stem and -ity as the abstract ending: usefulness turned into a noun.
normalIntro.cn: 把 util- 看成「有用」词干，把 -ity 看成抽象词尾：有用性做成了名词。

normal.en: Public utility names a company rather than a quality.
normal.cn: public utility 指的是公司，不是某种性质。

normal.en: Utility bill is the household phrase for water, gas, and power charges.
normal.cn: utility bill 是家里的水电煤气账单。

normal.en: Utilize and utility share one stem, one verb and one noun.
normal.cn: utilize 与 utility 同词干，一个是动词，一个是名词。

normal.en: A utility room is a plain working room, not a beautiful one.
normal.cn: utility room 是朴素的干活房，不是好看的房间。

normal.en: In economics the plural utilities is rarely used; the sense stays abstract.
normal.cn: 经济学里几乎不用复数，那一层意义始终是抽象的。

abstract.en: Picture a row of meters on a wall, quietly counting water and power.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上一排表，安静地数着水与电。

abstract.en: Open an envelope with a utility bill inside and see the winter figure.
abstract.cn: 拆开一个信封，看见里面冬季的水电单。

abstract.en: Watch a small disk program clean a cluttered drive.
abstract.cn: 看一个小小的磁盘程序清理杂乱的硬盘。

examples.en: The chief utility of the map is that it folds into a pocket.
examples.cn: 这张地图的主要实用之处是能折进口袋。

examples.en: The family cut its utility costs by half last winter.
examples.cn: 这家人在去年冬天把水电煤气费削减了一半。

examples.en: The building stands on land once owned by the local utility.
examples.cn: 这栋楼盖在曾属于当地公用事业公司的土地上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「优体利体」——身体用起来又优又利，说的还是有用。

root: 拉丁语 uti（使用）→ utilis（有用的）→ utilitas（有用性），经古法语 utilité 进入英语

sensesIntro.en: The abstract quality of being useful narrows to a particular function, widens to public services, and is borrowed by computing and economics.
sensesIntro.cn: 「有用」这一抽象性质先收窄为具体功用，再扩大为公用事业，又被计算机与经济学术语借用。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of meters counting invisible supply.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排计量表记录着看不见的供给。

branches.en: The quality branch: usefulness as a property of things.
branches.cn: 性质分支：作为事物属性的有用性。

branches.en: The function branch: the job a thing can still do.
branches.cn: 功用分支：某物还能担任的那项职能。

branches.en: The service branch: gas, water, and power as businesses.
branches.cn: 服务分支：作为企业的燃气、水与电力。

branches.en: The software branch: a program valued for its function.
branches.cn: 软件分支：以功能取胜的程序。

branches.en: The economic branch: usefulness made countable.
branches.cn: 经济分支：被变成可计量的用处。

intro.en: A Latin stem of use, a linking -il-, and the abstract ending -ity: usefulness as a noun.
intro.cn: 拉丁语「使用」词干，加连接成分 -il-，再加抽象词尾 -ity：把有用性做成名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin uti, to use, gives utilis, useful, and utilitas, usefulness; the ending -itas becomes English -ity.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 uti（使用）给出 utilis（有用的）与 utilitas（有用性）；词尾 -itas 变成英语 -ity。

items.example: The verb uti is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 动词 uti 是整个词族的根。

items.example: The stem util- appears in utility and utilize.
items.exampleCN: 词干 util- 见于 utility 与 utilize。

items.example: Utility names a quality.
Utilize is the matching verb.
Utilitarian adds a label for a way of thinking.
items.exampleCN: utilitarian 加上了思想取向的标签。

items.example: Utilization means the act of putting to use.
Use is the everyday cousin of uti.
items.exampleCN: use 是 uti 的日常对应词。

items.example: A public utility serves a whole town.
items.exampleCN: public utility 服务整个城镇。

definition_zh: 利用；运用；使用
definition_en: to make practical use of something, especially in a way that puts it to good purpose
core_image: 把废木料锯开钉成一张结实的书架
scene: 院子里堆着装修拆下的旧木板，木匠量了量，决定把它们做成靠墙的架子。They utilized every scrap of timber on the site.
sceneCN: 这里 utilize 是「利用」（第 1 个义项：把已有的东西拿来派上用场）；句意为他们把工地上每一块零碎木料都利用了起来。旧木料变成书架的画面，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 加名词后缀 -ation，义为「利用；使用」
同根名词，义为「效用；公用事业」
同根形容词，义为「实用的；功利的」
同义形容词，义为「可用的」

senses.title: To put something to practical use
senses.definition: to find a practical use for something that exists
senses.definitionCN: 为已有的东西找到实际用途
senses.example: The school utilized the old hall as a library.
senses.exampleCN: 学校把旧礼堂改作图书馆使用。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to use, and the suffix makes an English verb; together they add the idea of turning something to good account.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「使用」，后缀让它成为英语动词；合起来带上「把事情办得其所」的意味。

senses.title: To employ existing resources
senses.definition: to make efficient use of available supplies, money, or space
senses.definitionCN: 高效地使用现有的物资、资金或空间
senses.example: The team utilized the spare room for meetings.
senses.exampleCN: 团队把闲置的房间用来开会。
senses.why: Where supplies are limited, using them well became the point of the word, and efficiency lies in the background of this sense.
senses.whyCN: 物资有限时「把东西用得好」成了重点，这层意思背后始终有理性的计算。

senses.title: To adopt a method or skill
senses.definition: to adopt a technique or skill for a particular task
senses.definitionCN: 为某项任务采用一种技术或技能
senses.example: The hospital utilizes a new method of scanning.
senses.exampleCN: 这家医院采用了一种新的扫描方法。
senses.why: Methods and skills are abstract tools, and anything that can be put to work fits the same frame.
senses.whyCN: 方法与技能是抽象的「工具」，凡能拿来干活的东西都套进同一个框架。

senses.title: In formal writing, simply to use
senses.definition: used in formal or technical writing simply where use would be plainer
senses.definitionCN: 在正式或技术性文字中替代更朴素的 use
senses.example: The report utilizes the term risk in two ways.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告以两种含义使用了风险一词。
senses.why: Formal style likes longer borrowed verbs, so the word often stands in for plain use without adding much.
senses.whyCN: 正式文体偏爱较长的借入动词，于是这个词常只当作 use 的替代，并未添多少新意。

intro.en: A formal English verb built in modern times from the Latin noun utilitas, useful.
intro.cn: 一个近代在英语中构造的正式动词，取自拉丁名词 utilitas（有用的）。

items.en: Uti meant to use, and utilis meant useful, with utilitas naming usefulness.
items.cn: uti 意为使用，utilis 意为有用的，utilitas 指有用性。

items.en: Utiliser appeared in French in the eighteenth century, built from the same Latin noun.
items.cn: utiliser 于十八世纪出现在法语中，同样由这个拉丁名词构造。

items.en: English forms utilize in the nineteenth century, following the French pattern.
items.cn: 英语循法语模式在十九世纪造出 utilize。

items.en: Technical writing takes it up at once for the efficient use of resources.
items.cn: 技术写作立刻采用它来表示资源的有效利用。

items.en: Modern style guides advise readers to prefer plain use where meaning is the same.
items.cn: 现代文风指南建议读者在意思相同时选用更朴素的 use。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the util- stem, and the near-meaning group separates plain use from efficient exploitation.
note.cn: 形近组共享 util- 词干，近义组则把朴素的 use 与高效的利用区分开。

entries.definition: the act of putting to use
to use a method or tool
to fail to use something well

normalIntro.en: Read it as utility turned into a verb: to make the useful quality happen.
normalIntro.cn: 把它看成 utility 转成的动词：让「有用」这件事发生。

normal.en: The ending -ize marks it as a verb of making, like modernize and organize.
normal.cn: -ize 词尾标记这是「使……」类动词，如 modernize、organize。

normal.en: Utilize is formal; use is the everyday choice.
normal.cn: utilize 属正式用语，日常生活中用 use。

normal.en: Utilization is the noun, and it stays abstract.
normal.cn: 名词是 utilization，同样是抽象的。

normal.en: Widely utilized is a favourite passive phrase in reports.
normal.cn: widely utilized 是报告里最爱的被动说法。

normal.en: Utilize space and utilize resources are the two common objects.
normal.cn: 常见搭配对象是空间与资源。

abstract.en: Picture old planks cut and nailed into a shelf.
abstract.cn: 想象旧木板被锯开、钉成一只书架。

abstract.en: See rain water caught in a barrel for the garden.
abstract.cn: 看雨水被接进桶里浇园子。

abstract.en: Hear a report say the empty hall is now in use, though it says utilize.
abstract.cn: 听报告说空礼堂现已投入使用，只是用了 utilize 这个词。

examples.en: The chef utilizes every part of the vegetable, down to the leaves.
examples.cn: 这位厨师把蔬菜的每一部分都利用起来，连叶子也不放过。

examples.en: Solar panels let the farm utilize its own roof space.
examples.cn: 太阳能板让农场利用起了自己的屋顶空间。

examples.en: The study utilizes data collected over ten years.
examples.cn: 这项研究运用了十年间收集的数据。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「优体来用」——好东西来了就用上，别搁着积灰。

root: 拉丁语 uti（使用）→ utilis（有用的）→ utilitas（有用性）；法语 utiliser 于十八世纪构造，英语十九世纪仿此造出 utilize

sensesIntro.en: A formal verb for putting things to use spreads to resources, to methods and skills, and to plain stylistic replacement for use.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个正式动词从「把东西用起来」扩展到资源、方法与技能，也成了 use 的文风替代品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: scrap planks cut and nailed into a shelf.
core.cn: 核心意象：废木料被锯开、钉成书架。

branches.en: The use branch: something idle is given a job.
branches.cn: 使用分支：闲置之物被派上了活。

branches.en: The resource branch: supplies, money, and space used well.
branches.cn: 资源分支：物资、资金、空间被用好。

branches.en: The method branch: a technique adopted for a task.
branches.cn: 方法分支：为某项任务采用的技术。

branches.en: The style branch: a longer word where use would do.
branches.cn: 文风分支：本可用 use 时换成更长的词。

branches.en: The efficiency branch: nothing is left lying unused.
branches.cn: 效率分支：不让任何东西白白闲置。

intro.en: The useful stem plus a verb ending of making: to make something useful in practice.
intro.cn: 「有用」词干加表示「使……」的动词词尾：让某物实际有用起来。

latinIntro.en: From Latin utilis, useful, built on uti, to use; the English verb ending -ize comes through French -iser.
latinIntro.cn: 源自拉丁语 utilis（有用的），由 uti（使用）构成；英语动词词尾 -ize 经法语 -iser 而来。

items.example: The stem util- ties the family together.
items.exampleCN: 词干 util- 把这一词族联在一起。

items.example: Utilize turns usefulness into action.
Utilization is the act itself.
Utility names the quality being used.
items.exampleCN: utility 命名被使用的那种性质。

items.example: Utilitarian labels a philosophical outlook.
items.exampleCN: utilitarian 标记一种思想立场。

items.example: Use is the short native-style partner.
items.exampleCN: use 是短小的日常伙伴。

items.example: Employ is a formal rival of utilize.
items.exampleCN: employ 是 utilize 的正式竞争对手。

items.example: Exploit suggests full use for profit.
items.exampleCN: exploit 暗示为获利而充分利用。

definition_zh: 极度的；最大的；最远的；极限
definition_en: of the greatest degree or amount, or the furthest possible point
core_image: 绳子绕到最后一圈，已经退到崖边再无可退
scene: 攀岩者背着伤员往下撤，绳子已经绷到最后一圈，面前只剩几步可走。They treated the injured climber with the utmost care.
sceneCN: 这里 utmost 是「极度的、最大的」（第 1 个义项：程度达到极限）；句意为他们以最小心谨慎的方式照料那名受伤的攀岩者。绳子绕到最后一圈的画面，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 同源变体，义为「最远的；极度的」
同根副词，义为「完全地；彻底地」
同源比较级，义为「外面的」
同源变体，义为「最外的」

senses.title: The greatest possible degree
senses.definition: used of a quality at the highest degree possible
senses.definitionCN: 形容某种性质达到可能达到的最高程度
senses.example: The matter is of the utmost importance to the family.
senses.exampleCN: 这件事对这家人来说极其重要。
senses.why: The word began as the outermost point on a scale, so anything at that far end is at its greatest possible degree.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本义是刻度上最外的一端点，因此处在那一点上的东西就达到了可能的最高程度。

senses.title: The furthest possible effort
senses.definition: used in the phrase do one's utmost, to try as hard as one can
senses.definitionCN: 用于 do one's utmost，表示尽最大所能
senses.example: She did her utmost to keep the meeting calm.
senses.exampleCN: 她竭尽全力让会议保持平静。
senses.why: If the outermost point is the limit, then to act to that point is to give everything one has.
senses.whyCN: 既然最外之点就是界限，那么把行动推到那一点，就是把所有力气都拿出来。

senses.title: The extreme limit as a noun
senses.definition: as a noun, the greatest extent of something such as power or effort
senses.definitionCN: 作名词时指权力、努力等的最大范围
senses.example: The engines were pushed to the utmost.
senses.exampleCN: 发动机被开到了极限。
senses.why: The adjective's far end becomes a thing in itself, and people speak of the utmost as a boundary they reach.
senses.whyCN: 形容词所指的最外端点本身成了名词，人们便说「到了极限」这样一个被触及的边界。

senses.title: Carest and most attentive
senses.definition: used of attention or care that could not be exceeded
senses.definitionCN: 形容关照或小心已无以复加
senses.example: The old manuscripts were handled with the utmost care.
senses.exampleCN: 那些古旧手稿被极其小心地对待。
senses.why: Care also has degrees, and the outermost degree is the one that cannot be increased further.
senses.whyCN: 关照同样有程度之分，最外的那一档就是再无法增加的关照。

senses.title: Furthest away in place
senses.definition: describing the point furthest away or the end of an area
senses.definitionCN: 形容最远的点或一块区域的尽头
senses.example: They planted trees along the utmost edge of the field.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在田地的尽头边缘种了树。
senses.why: The spatial sense is the oldest one, and the figurative senses of degree grew out of it.
senses.whyCN: 空间上的「最外」是最老的用法，程度上的引申义正是从这里长出来的。

intro.en: A double superlative in form: the old word out with the ending -most on top, meaning the outermost point.
intro.cn: 形式上是个双重最高级：古老的 out 加上最高级词尾 -most，意为「最外的那个点」。

items.en: Utmest and ytemest were formed from ut, out, with the superlative ending -mest.
items.cn: utmost 的古形 utmest、ytemest 由 ut（向外）加最高级词尾 -mest 构成。

items.en: The neighbouring Norse form útmastr with the same meaning reinforced the English word.
items.cn: 邻近的古诺尔斯语形式 útmastr 意义相同，强化了英语这一构词。

items.en: The word is used for the furthest edge of a place or a piece of land.
items.cn: 中古英语时期，这个词用来指某地或某块土地最远的边缘。

items.en: From the physical edge the word moves to the extreme of qualities such as care and importance.
items.cn: 从实体的边缘，这个词转向关照、重要性等性质的极限。

items.en: The phrase do one's utmost fixes the noun use in ordinary speech.
items.cn: do one's utmost 这个说法把名词用法固定在日常口语中。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the old out family, and the near-meaning group gathers words for extremes.
note.cn: 形近组收集古老的 out 词族，近义组汇集表示极致的一类词。

entries.definition: completely, with the same old stem, though the meaning has shifted
entries.definitionCN: 完全地；同出古词干，词义已偏移

entries.definition: at the very end of a scale

normalIntro.en: See it as out plus -most: the most out you can go, and therefore the furthest degree.
normalIntro.cn: 把它看成 out 加 -most：能往外走到的最远处，也就是最大的程度。

normal.en: Utmost appears in fixed phrases such as the utmost care and the utmost respect.
normal.cn: utmost 常见于 the utmost care、the utmost respect 等固定搭配。

normal.en: Do one's utmost is the standard idiom for trying one's hardest.
normal.cn: do one's utmost 是「竭尽全力」的标准习语。

normal.en: Uttermost is an older variant with the same sense.
normal.cn: uttermost 是意义相同的旧变体。

normal.en: The word is nearly always used with the, not with a.
normal.cn: 这个词几乎总与 the 连用，而不与 a 连用。

normal.en: Utterly descends from the same old stem but now means completely.
normal.cn: utterly 同出这一古老词干，但今天意为「完全」。

abstract.en: Picture a rope paying out to its last coil at the cliff edge.
abstract.cn: 想象绳子放到崖边的最后一圈。

abstract.en: Hear the engineers push a machine to its loudest, hottest limit.
abstract.cn: 听工程师把机器推到最响最热的极限。

abstract.en: Give your last ounce of strength to hold a door shut.
abstract.cn: 用最后一点力气把门顶住。

examples.en: The documents were handled with the utmost care.
examples.cn: 这些文件被极其小心地处理。

examples.en: He did his utmost to explain the delay to the passengers.
examples.cn: 他竭尽全力向乘客解释延误的原因。

examples.en: Safety is of the utmost importance on the building site.
examples.cn: 在工地上安全是最重要的事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「压到末寺」——被压到寺庙最后一角，已是退无可退的极限。

root: 古英语 ut（向外）加最高级词尾 -mest 构成 utmest，受古诺尔斯语 útmastr 影响定型为 utmost，本义「最外的点」

sensesIntro.en: One spatial edge gives the greatest degree, then the full effort, then the limit as a noun, then the care beyond which nothing can go.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个空间边缘先给出最大程度，再给出全力，再给出作为名词的极限，最后是再无法增加的关照。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rope out to its last coil at the cliff edge.
core.cn: 核心意象：绳子放到崖边最后一圈。

branches.en: The degree branch: a quality at its highest.
branches.cn: 程度分支：某种性质的最高档。

branches.en: The effort branch: giving everything one has.
branches.cn: 努力分支：把所有的都给出去。

branches.en: The noun branch: the limit becomes a place to reach.
branches.cn: 名词分支：极限成了可以被触及的位置。

branches.en: The care branch: attention that cannot be increased.
branches.cn: 关照分支：再无法增加的用心。

branches.en: The space branch: the oldest, most literal edge.
branches.cn: 空间分支：最古老、最直白的边缘义。

intro.en: An old Germanic adverb of direction takes a superlative ending; there is no Latin element inside.
intro.cn: 一个古老的日耳曼方位副词加上最高级词尾，里面没有拉丁成分。

latinIntro.en: The word is wholly Germanic, so there is no Latin cognate family to list; the comparable Latin root would be extra, outside.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词完全属于日耳曼语系，没有可列的拉丁同族词；可作参照的拉丁词根是 extra（在外面）。

items.example: Ut- is the old form of out.
items.exampleCN: ut- 是 out 的古老形式。

items.example: The ending marks the extreme point.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾标记最远的端点。

items.example: Out is the modern form of the same word.
items.exampleCN: out 是同一个词的现代形式。

items.structure: related word with a different meaning
items.example: Utterly descends from the same stem.
Outer keeps the old stem in a plain adjective.
items.exampleCN: outer 把这一词干保存在普通形容词里。

items.example: The quality can be named abstractly if needed.
items.exampleCN: 必要时可以把这一性质抽象成名词。

items.example: Inmost follows the same -most pattern.
items.exampleCN: inmost 走的是同一个 -most 模式。

items.example: Topmost again shows -most at work.
items.exampleCN: topmost 再一次显示 -most 的构词力。

definition_zh: 说出；发出（声音）；完全的；彻底的
definition_en: to say something or make a sound, or used of a complete state with nothing else mixed in
core_image: 一个人低声吐出两个字，声音轻得几乎听不见
scene: 黑暗里两个人靠墙坐着，其中一人终于开口，只吐出一句简短的道歉。She was too tired to utter a single word.
sceneCN: 这里 utter 是「说出、发出」（第 1 个义项：用声音把话说出来）；句意为她累得一个字也说不出来。黑暗里轻轻吐出几个字的画面，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 加名词后缀 -ance，义为「话语；言论」
加 -ly 构成副词，义为「完全地」
同源词，义为「最远的；极度的」
同源词，义为「向外」

senses.title: To say something aloud
senses.definition: to say a word or a sentence, especially something short or final
senses.definitionCN: 说出一个词或一句话，尤指短促或决定性的话
senses.example: He did not utter a single word during the trial.
senses.exampleCN: 整个审判过程中他一个字也没说。
senses.why: The oldest form of the word meant putting out, and the voice puts breath and words out of the mouth.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的意思是「向外送出」，而声音正是把气息与话语从口中送出。

senses.title: To make a sound
senses.definition: to make a sound with the voice or with something else
senses.definitionCN: 用嗓音或别的东西发出声响
senses.example: The bird uttered a low whistle from the hedge.
senses.exampleCN: 那只鸟从树篱里发出一声低低的哨音。
senses.why: Once uttering means sending out breath, any sound can be sent out the same way.
senses.whyCN: 既然「说出」是把气息送出去，那么任何声音都可以照样送出去。

senses.title: Complete, with nothing else
senses.definition: used as an adjective of a state that is total, often with bad nouns
senses.definitionCN: 作形容词时形容某种状态是十足的，常与负面名词连用
senses.example: There was utter silence when the result was read out.
senses.exampleCN: 结果被念出时，一片寂静。
senses.why: The adjectival use follows the sense of going all the way out, so it means complete to the outermost degree.
senses.whyCN: 形容词用法承自「一直送到最外」的意思，所以它表示完整到了极点。

senses.title: The most complete kind of something
senses.definition: strengthening a noun such as failure or nonsense
senses.definitionCN: 用来加强失败、胡言这类名词的语气
senses.example: Calling the whole plan nonsense was an utter waste of a meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 把整个计划说成胡言，是白白浪费了一场会。
senses.why: Utter is almost never used for good nouns, so the adjective doubles as a signal of strong disapproval.
senses.whyCN: 这个词几乎不用在褒义名词上，因此这名形容词也成了强烈不赞同的信号。

intro.en: Two old senses, to send out and outermost, grew from the same Germanic root and have kept the same spelling.
intro.cn: 「向外送出」与「最外」两个古老意思都出自同一个日耳曼词根，并且拼写一直相同。

items.en: Uttrian meant to put out or drive out, from the adverb ut, out.
items.cn: uttrian 意为「放出、赶出」，来自副词 ut（向外）。

items.en: Utter and uttera meant outer, from the comparative of ut.
items.cn: utter 与 uttera 意为「外面的」，来自 ut 的比较级。

items.en: The verb extends from driving things out to giving voice to words.
items.cn: 这个动词从「把东西赶出去」扩展到「把话说出来」。

items.en: The adjective settles into the sense of complete, mostly before nouns of failure or silence.
items.cn: 形容词固定为「完全的」之义，多用在失败、寂静一类名词之前。

items.en: Utterance and utterly are the two surviving derivations in everyday use.
items.cn: utterance 与 utterly 是日常里留下的两个派生词。

note.en: The look-alike group shows the old out stem, and the near-meaning group divides speaking from complete states.
note.cn: 形近组展示古老的 out 词干，近义组按「说出」与「完全」两类意义分开。

entries.definition: to make the sound of a word

normalIntro.en: One short word hides two lives: saying something aloud, and being complete to the last degree.
normalIntro.cn: 一个短词藏着两种生命：把话说出声来，以及完整到极点。

normal.en: Not utter a word is the fixed negative idiom.
normal.cn: not utter a word 是固定的否定说法。

normal.en: As an adjective it prefers bad nouns: utter nonsense and utter failure.
normal.cn: 作形容词时偏爱负面名词：utter nonsense、utter failure。

normal.en: Utterance is the noun, utterly the adverb.
normal.cn: 名词是 utterance，副词是 utterly。

normal.en: The adjective has no comparative form in normal use.
normal.cn: 这个形容词在正常用法中没有比较级。

normal.en: The same stem gives out and utmost, all pointing outward.
normal.cn: 同一词干给出 out 与 utmost，都指向「向外」。

abstract.en: Picture a whisper pressed out through the lips in a dark room.
abstract.cn: 想象黑暗房间里一句话被嘴唇轻轻挤出。

abstract.en: Hear total silence after a verdict is read.
abstract.cn: 听判决念完之后那种彻底的安静。

abstract.en: See a plan collapse from the very first step.
abstract.cn: 看一个计划从第一步就彻底垮掉。

examples.en: He was so shocked that he could not utter a word.
examples.cn: 他震惊得一个字也说不出来。

examples.en: The meeting ended in utter silence.
examples.cn: 会议在一片彻底的沉默中结束。

examples.en: Everyone agreed the rumour was utter nonsense.
examples.cn: 大家都认同那传闻纯属胡言。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿特」——阿特一开口，说出的话就是十足的直白。

root: 古英语 ut（向外）：动词 uttrian（放出、说出）与形容词 uttera（外面的、彻底的）同出一源

sensesIntro.en: Sending breath outward gives the verb of speaking and of any sound, while the outward edge gives the adjective of complete states.
sensesIntro.cn: 把气息向外送出给出「说」与「发声」的动词义，而「最外之端」给出「彻底的」这一形容词义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: words pushed out through the lips in the dark.
core.cn: 核心意象：黑暗里几个字被嘴唇挤出来。

branches.en: The speech branch: one word put out into the air.
branches.cn: 言语分支：一个字被送到空气里。

branches.en: The sound branch: voice or whistle sent out.
branches.cn: 声音分支：嗓音或哨音被送出。

branches.en: The adjective branch: a state complete to the edge.
branches.cn: 形容词分支：完整到边界的某种状态。

branches.en: The judgement branch: complete, and therefore strongly negative.
branches.cn: 评判分支：彻底，因而强烈否定。

branches.en: The breath branch: both speech and sound ride on outgoing breath.
branches.cn: 气息分支：说话与发声都靠呼出的气息。

intro.en: A Germanic root meaning outward, with no Latin inside; the two senses split early.
intro.cn: 一个意为「向外」的日耳曼词根，内部没有拉丁成分；两个义项很早就分开了。

latinIntro.en: The word has no Latin ancestor; the nearest Latin idea is the adverb extra, outside, which is listed for comparison only.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语祖源；最接近的拉丁概念是副词 extra（在外面），此处仅供对照。

items.example: The old root ut- means out.
items.exampleCN: 古老词根 ut- 意为向外。

items.example: Utter comes from driving something out.
items.exampleCN: utter 源自把东西送出去。

items.example: The verb ending marks the everyday action.
items.exampleCN: 动词词尾标记日常的反复动作。

items.example: Utterance is something said.
Utterly means to the full degree.
items.exampleCN: utterly 意为达到完全的程度。

items.example: Out is the plain modern form.
items.exampleCN: out 是这个词的现代朴素形式。

items.example: Utmost shares the root.
Inmost is its inward twin.
items.exampleCN: inmost 是它内在的对称词。

definition_zh: 空的；空缺的；空闲的；茫然的
definition_en: empty and not occupied, free for someone to take, or showing no thought
core_image: 一间搬空的屋子，只剩地上一块没被晒褪色的方印
scene: 楼下的门上贴着招租的纸条，窗帘全拆了，从街上能看见里面空荡的墙。The flat has been vacant since the family left in spring.
sceneCN: 这里 vacant 是「空的、无人居住的」（第 1 个义项：无人占用）；句意为这家人春天搬走后，这套房子一直空着。搬空屋子里的方印，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 加抽象名词后缀 -cy，义为「空缺；空房」
加 -ly 构成副词，义为「茫然地」
同根动词，义为「腾出；空出」
同根名词，义为「假期」

senses.title: Empty and not occupied
senses.definition: of a room, seat, or building, empty because nobody is using it
senses.definitionCN: 形容房间、座位或建筑无人使用而空着
senses.example: The seat beside her stayed vacant for the whole journey.
senses.exampleCN: 旅途中她旁边的座位一直空着。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to be empty or free, and the adjective simply names that state of being left unoccupied.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「空着、闲置」，形容词只是把这种无人占用的状态命名出来。

senses.title: A job or position with nobody in it
senses.definition: of a job or post that no one holds at present
senses.definitionCN: 形容某个职位目前无人担任
senses.example: The manager's post fell vacant in June.
senses.exampleCN: 经理一职在六月空了出来。
senses.why: A post is like a seat in an office: when the holder leaves, the place stays empty and waits to be filled.
senses.whyCN: 职位就像办公室里的一把椅子：任职者走了，位置就空在那里等有人补上。

senses.title: Free from duties, unoccupied time
senses.definition: of time or a person, free from work or duty
senses.definitionCN: 形容时间或人没有工作与职责在身
senses.example: In his vacant hours he walks along the canal.
senses.exampleCN: 空闲的时候他就沿着运河散步。
senses.why: If the space is empty, the person is free; the word transfers easily from places to hours and to people.
senses.whyCN: 空间空着，人也就被腾出来了；这个词很容易从地方转到时间与人身上。

senses.title: Showing no thought or interest
senses.definition: of a look or expression that shows no thought or attention
senses.definitionCN: 形容眼神或表情里没有想法与注意
senses.example: He gave a vacant stare when asked about the date.
senses.exampleCN: 问他日子时，他茫然地瞪着眼。
senses.why: An empty room has nothing in it, and a face with nothing behind it looks the same way, so the word crosses over.
senses.whyCN: 空屋子里面什么都没有，面上背后什么都没有的样子也一样，于是词义就这么挪了过去。

senses.title: Of no force, empty of effect
senses.definition: in legal and formal use, having no force or holder
senses.definitionCN: 在法律与正式用语中，指没有效力或没有持有者
senses.example: The promise was vacant because nothing was signed.
senses.exampleCN: 因为什么都没签，那句承诺并无实效。
senses.why: Law borrows the plain idea of emptiness to say that a right or a promise has nothing inside it.
senses.whyCN: 法律借用了最朴素的「空」来说明某项权利或诺言里面没有实质内容。

intro.en: From Latin vacare, to be empty, through French; the same root gives vacation and vacuum.
intro.cn: 来自拉丁语 vacare（空着），经法语进入英语；同一词根也给出 vacation 与 vacuum。

items.en: Vacare meant to be empty, free, or at leisure, and vacans was its present participle.
items.cn: vacare 意为「空着、自由、有闲」，vacans 是它的现在分词。

items.en: Vacant entered French as a legal word for property and offices with no holder.
items.cn: vacant 作为法律用词进入法语，指无人占有的产业与职位。

items.en: English borrows the word in the fourteenth century, first for empty land and posts.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入这个词，最初用于空地与空缺职位。

items.en: The phrase vacant possession fixes the sense of an empty house handed over.
items.cn: vacant possession 这一说法固定了「交房时已腾空」的含义。

items.en: From empty rooms the word passes to blank expressions and to rights with no force.
items.cn: 从空房间出发，词义又转到茫然的神情与没有效力的权利上。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the vac- family, and the near-meaning group contrasts empty with occupied and busy.
note.cn: 形近组收集 vac- 词族，近义组把空着与占用、忙碌对照起来。

entries.definition: an empty room or unfilled job
a space with no matter in it
free to be taken or used

normalIntro.en: One Latin idea of being empty runs through the vac- family: vacant, vacancy, vacate, vacation, vacuum.
normalIntro.cn: 「空着」这一个拉丁概念贯穿 vac- 词族：vacant、vacancy、vacate、vacation、vacuum。

normal.en: A vacant post and a vacant seat both mean a place waiting for someone.
normal.cn: vacant post 与 vacant seat 都指等着人来的位置。

normal.en: A vacant look is the figurative use and very common in novels.
normal.cn: vacant look 是引申用法，在小说里十分常见。

normal.en: Vacancy is the noun for both an empty room and an unfilled job.
normal.cn: vacancy 既是空房，也是空缺职位。

normal.en: The verb vacate is the action behind the adjective.
normal.cn: 形容词背后的动作就是动词 vacate。

normal.en: Hotels say no vacancy when every room is taken.
normal.cn: 旅馆满房时会说 no vacancy。

abstract.en: Picture a bare room with a pale square where a picture hung.
abstract.cn: 想象空屋子里墙上留下一块没褪色的方印。

abstract.en: Hear a landlord tape a renting notice to a door.
abstract.cn: 听房东往门上贴招租纸条。

abstract.en: See someone answer a question with eyes that focus on nothing.
abstract.cn: 看有人回答问题时眼神落在空处。

examples.en: There are two vacant rooms on the second floor.
examples.cn: 二楼有两个空房间。

examples.en: The teaching post has been vacant since last summer.
examples.cn: 这个教职从去年夏天起一直空着。

examples.en: He stared at the map with a vacant expression.
examples.cn: 他茫然地盯着地图。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「未垦」——还没被开垦的地荒着，也就是空着没人用。

root: 拉丁语 vacare（空着、有闲）的现在分词 vacans，经古法语 vacant 进入英语

sensesIntro.en: Empty space, then an unfilled post, then free time, then a face with nothing behind it, and finally a right with no force.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是空出的地方，再是没人担任的职位，再是空出的时间，再是背后空无一物的表情，最后是没有效力的权利。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bare room with a pale square on the wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：空屋子里墙上那块浅色方印。

branches.en: The space branch: a place with nobody using it.
branches.cn: 空间分支：没人使用的地方。

branches.en: The job branch: a working place waiting to be filled.
branches.cn: 职位分支：等待补人的工作岗位。

branches.en: The time branch: hours with no duty attached.
branches.cn: 时间分支：没有职责的小时。

branches.en: The face branch: eyes with nothing focused on them.
branches.cn: 表情分支：目光没有落点。

branches.en: The formal branch: emptiness in law and in offices.
branches.cn: 正式分支：法律与职位上的「空」。

intro.en: A Latin root of emptiness with an adjective ending: literally being empty.
intro.cn: 一个表示「空」的拉丁词根加形容词词尾：字面就是「空着的」。

latinIntro.en: Latin vacare, to be empty or at leisure, gives vacans and the noun vacatio; the endings -ant and -ance are its English forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vacare（空着、有闲）给出 vacans 与名词 vacatio；英语形式为词尾 -ant 与 -ance。

items.example: The root vac- carries emptiness.
items.exampleCN: 词根 vac- 承载「空」义。

items.example: Vacant means being empty.
items.exampleCN: vacant 意为处于空着的状态。

items.example: Vacancy names the empty state or room.
items.exampleCN: vacancy 命名空着的状态或房间。

items.example: Vacate means to make a place empty.
Vacation once meant the act of vacating.
items.exampleCN: vacation 早先指腾空这一行为。

items.example: Vacantly describes a blank stare.
Vacuum is a Latin-style noun of emptiness.
items.exampleCN: vacuum 是拉丁式的「空」名词。

items.example: Empty is the native-style partner.

latinEntries.meaning: to be empty, to be free

definition_zh: 假期；度假；休庭期
definition_en: a period of time away from work or school, often spent travelling
core_image: 行李箱敞在床上，一半是泳衣一半是防晒霜
scene: 七月的最后一天，办公室的灯一盏盏关掉，同事把文件夹压在桌上，说下周谁也不许找他。They spent their vacation on a quiet island.
sceneCN: 这里 vacation 是「假期」（第 1 个义项：离开工作或学习的休假期）；句意为他们在一个安静的小岛上度假。敞开的行李箱，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 同根动词，义为「腾出；空出」
同根形容词，义为「空的；空缺的」
同根名词，义为「空缺；空房」
加 -er 构成，义为「度假者」

senses.title: Time away from work or school
senses.definition: a period of some days or weeks when work or school stops
senses.definitionCN: 工作或学习停顿的一段天数或周数
senses.example: They took a three-week vacation in the mountains.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在山里休了三周假。
senses.why: The Latin noun first named a being free of duties, so the holiday is simply the period when those duties are lifted.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁名词最初指「免除职责」这一状态，所以假期就是职责被撤下的那段时间。

senses.title: A trip taken during such time
senses.definition: used of travelling or resting away from home during a holiday
senses.definitionCN: 指在假期里离家旅行或休息
senses.example: The whole family spent the vacation by the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 一家人整个假期都待在海边。
senses.why: Once the days are free, the journey that fills them takes the same name, and the trip becomes the vacation.
senses.whyCN: 日子一旦空出来，填满它的旅程也取了同样的名字，旅行本身就成了 vacation。

senses.title: A break granted by a court or office
senses.definition: a fixed break for a court or an institution
senses.definitionCN: 法院或机构固定的休止期
senses.example: The court is in vacation until early September.
senses.exampleCN: 法院休庭到九月初。
senses.why: Institutions also empty out for fixed weeks, so law keeps the word for the bench left sitting idle.
senses.whyCN: 机构也会在固定的几周里空下来，法律便用这个词指闲着的法官席。

senses.title: The act of giving up a post
senses.definition: in older use, the act of vacating a position or a place
senses.definitionCN: 旧时用法，指辞去或腾出一个职位、一处场所
senses.example: His vacation of the chair left the office empty for a year.
senses.exampleCN: 他辞去这一席位，让该职位空了一年。
senses.why: This is the oldest legal sense: the act of making a place empty by leaving it.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的法律义：离开一处场所，从而使它空出来。

intro.en: A Latin noun of exemption from duty, whose root also gives vacant and vacuum.
intro.cn: 一个表示「免除职责」的拉丁名词，其词根也给出 vacant 与 vacuum。

items.en: Vacare meant to be free of duty, and vacatio named the state of being exempt.
items.cn: vacare 意为「免于职责」，vacatio 指处于免除状态。

items.en: In legal use vacatio covered the free days of courts, when no case was heard.
items.cn: 在法律用语中，vacatio 指法院不审案的空闲日子。

items.en: Vacation carried the legal and ecclesiastical sense into French.
items.cn: vacation 把法律与教会的这层含义带进法语。

items.en: English borrows the word in the fourteenth century, first for the law courts and the universities.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入这个词，最初用于法院与大学。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the word names the ordinary holiday of any worker.
items.cn: 自十九世纪起，这个词泛指任何工作者的普通假期。

note.en: The look-alike group shows the vac- family of freedom and emptiness, and the near-meaning group places rest beside work.
note.cn: 形近组展示表示「空、自由」的 vac- 词族，近义组把休息与工作相对照。

entries.definition: a calling to a kind of work, only the ending is close, the root is different
entries.definitionCN: 职业；只是词尾相近，词源不同

entries.definition: the working part of a school year

normalIntro.en: A vacation is literally an emptying of the calendar: the days are cleared and left free.
normalIntro.cn: vacation 字面上就是把日历腾空：日子被清出来，空着。

normal.en: Go on vacation and take a vacation are the two set phrases.
normal.cn: go on vacation 与 take a vacation 是两个固定说法。

normal.en: American English says vacation where British English says holiday.
normal.cn: 美式说 vacation，英式说 holiday。

normal.en: The legal sense survives in court in vacation.
normal.cn: 法律义仍留在 court in vacation 这样的说法里。

normal.en: The root vac- links vacation to vacant and vacancy.
normal.cn: 词根 vac- 把 vacation 与 vacant、vacancy 连起来。

normal.en: Vacationer is mainly American and means a traveller on holiday.
normal.cn: vacationer 主要是美式用法，指度假的游客。

abstract.en: Picture a suitcase half packed at the foot of a bed.
abstract.cn: 想象床脚一只装了一半的箱子。

abstract.en: See a desk calendar with two empty weeks crossed out in yellow.
abstract.cn: 看台历上被黄色涂掉的两个空周。

abstract.en: Hear the click of office lights going off one by one.
abstract.cn: 听办公室的灯一盏盏关掉的声音。

examples.en: We spent our vacation walking in the hills.
examples.cn: 我们假期在山里徒步。

examples.en: She booked two weeks of vacation in August.
examples.cn: 她订了八月两周的休假。

examples.en: The court will sit again after the long vacation.
examples.cn: 法院在长休庭期之后会再次开庭。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我会开心」——假期一到，我就会开心。

root: 拉丁语 vacare（空着、免于职责）→ vacatio（免除职务、空闲），经古法语 vacation 进入英语

sensesIntro.en: An emptying of duty becomes the free time, then the trip taken in it, then an institution's pause, and in old law a post given up.
sensesIntro.cn: 把职责腾空，先成空出的时间，再成填满它的旅行，再成机构的停歇，旧法里还指让出的职位。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a suitcase half packed on a bed.
core.cn: 核心意象：床上一只装了一半的行李箱。

branches.en: The leaving branch: walking out of the office.
branches.cn: 出发分支：走出办公室。

branches.en: The trip branch: a fortnight on an island.
branches.cn: 旅行分支：在岛上待两周。

branches.en: The court branch: the bench is empty in September.
branches.cn: 法院分支：九月里法官席空着。

branches.en: The old branch: the chair left without a holder.
branches.cn: 旧分支：席位无人担任。

branches.en: The blend: holiday and journey share one noun today.
branches.cn: 融合分支：今天假期与旅程共用一个名词。

intro.en: The Latin root of emptiness plus the noun ending of state: an emptied calendar.
intro.cn: 拉丁语「空」词根加表示状态的名词词尾：被腾空的日历。

latinIntro.en: Vacare, to be free, gives vacatio; the ending -atio becomes English -ation as in creation and relation.
latinIntro.cn: vacare（自由无事）给出 vacatio；词尾 -atio 在英语中变为 -ation，如 creation、relation。

items.example: Vacation is a time left free.
Creation and relation share the ending.
items.exampleCN: creation 与 relation 共用这一词尾。

items.example: The verb is vacate.
The adjective is vacant.
The parallel noun is vacancy.
Vacationer names the traveller.
Holiday comes from holy day.
Holiday keeps day at the end.

definition_zh: 真空；真空吸尘器；空白；用吸尘器清扫
definition_en: a space with no air or matter in it, a machine that cleans by suction, or a gap left empty
core_image: 玻璃罩里的空气被抽干，羽毛和硬币同时落地
scene: 物理课上，老师把羽毛和硬币放进玻璃罩，按下开关，空气嘶嘶被抽走，羽毛和硬币同时落到底。In a vacuum, a feather falls as fast as a coin.
sceneCN: 这里 vacuum 是「真空」（第 1 个义项：没有空气的空间）；句意为在真空里羽毛和硬币下落得一样快。玻璃罩里的空气被抽干，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 同根形容词，义为「空洞的；茫然的」
同根名词，义为「空洞；无内容」
同根形容词，义为「空的；空缺的」
同根名词，义为「假期」

senses.title: A space with no air or matter
senses.definition: an enclosed space from which air and other matter have been removed
senses.definitionCN: 被抽去空气与其他物质的封闭空间
senses.example: Sound cannot travel through a vacuum.
senses.exampleCN: 声音无法在真空中传播。
senses.why: The Latin noun meant an empty space, and physics simply kept that exact meaning for a space with nothing in it.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁名词本指空旷之处，物理学只是原样保留了这一含义，用来指里面什么都没有的空间。

senses.title: A machine that cleans by suction
senses.definition: an electrical machine that removes dust by sucking air through it
senses.definitionCN: 用抽气的方式把灰尘吸走的电器
senses.example: She ran the vacuum over the carpet twice.
senses.exampleCN: 她用吸尘器把地毯吸了两遍。
senses.why: A cleaner that works by creating a partial vacuum took the name of the emptiness it makes.
senses.whyCN: 一种靠制造局部真空来清扫的机器，干脆用它所造出的「空」来命名。

senses.title: An empty gap left by something missing
senses.definition: a state or place left empty after something important is lost
senses.definitionCN: 重要之物失去后留下的空荡状态或位置
senses.example: Retirement left a vacuum in the team.
senses.exampleCN: 退休在团队里留下了一片空白。
senses.why: If an empty space is the point, then a team missing its leader is an empty space too, and the metaphor needs no change of word.
senses.whyCN: 既然关键在「空出来的位置」，那么失去领头人的团队也是一处空位，比喻连词都不用换。

senses.title: To clean with a suction machine
senses.definition: to clean a floor or a surface with a vacuum cleaner
senses.definitionCN: 用吸尘器清洁地面或表面
senses.example: He vacuums the stairs every Saturday morning.
senses.exampleCN: 他每周六早上用吸尘器吸楼梯。
senses.why: The noun naming the machine turns into a verb once people start doing the job with it.
senses.whyCN: 一旦人们用这台机器干活，称呼机器的名词就变成了动词。

senses.title: In isolation from real conditions
senses.definition: in the phrase in a vacuum, meaning without any surrounding influence or context
senses.definitionCN: 用于 in a vacuum，指没有任何周围影响或情境
senses.example: No plan is made in a vacuum; every room has a budget.
senses.exampleCN: 任何计划都不是凭空定下的，每间屋子都有预算。
